title: How to choose a good rational basis for elliptic Feynman integrals?
description: 2-loop sunrise with masses m,M,m in d=2-2eps; elliptic. (Families D and TT of the paper are not usable: their propagators are only shown as graphs/in references, ancillary files contain bases and DEs but no propagator definitions.)
propagators_as_in_paper: rho_SR={l1^2-m^2, l2^2-M^2, (l1-l2-p)^2-m^2, l1.p, l2.p}; paper sets p^2=1
mapping_notes: Linear ISPs l1.p, l2.p replaced by quadratic aux lines (l1-p)^2 and (l2-p)^2. Conversion: l2.p=(D2+M^2+p^2-N5)/2 with N5=(l2-p)^2, so paper G^{1,1,1,0,-1} = 1/2[ G^{1,0,1,0,0} + (M^2+p^2) G^{1,1,1,0,0} - I_ours(1,1,1,0,-1) ]. Measure in paper: int prod d^d l (no normalization stated).

point.note: Euclidean point chosen by me (paper normalises p^2=1, generic m,M).

reference_notes: Paper gives only symbolic eps-expansions (eq.64-65), no numbers.
confidence: high for definition; low value as a benchmark (2-loop sunrise).
